questions.question_text:
Statements:
I. The prices of petrol and diesel in the domestic market have remained unchanged for the past few months.
II. The crude oil prices in the international market have gone up substantially in the last few months.
Choose the relationship between Statements I and II.

options.A: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect.
options.B: Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect.
options.C: Both statements are effects of some common cause.

questions.explanation: The statements report separate market observations. The source gives no policy or other link that establishes either statement as the cause of the other or identifies a common cause, so they are treated as independent effects.
questions.source: Analytical Reasoning 02_Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 5, Q1; Cause and Effect

questions.question_text:
Statements:
I. The government has recently fixed the fees for professional courses offered by unaided institutions at a level much lower than the fees charged last year.
II. The parents of aspiring students launched a severe agitation last year protesting against the high fees charged by the unaided institutions.
Choose the relationship between Statements I and II.

options.A: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect.
options.B: Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect.
options.C: Both statements are effects of some common cause.

questions.explanation: The parents' protest against high fees preceded the government's later fee reduction and gives a direct reason for that decision. The fee reduction cannot have caused an agitation that occurred the previous year.
questions.source: Analytical Reasoning 02_Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 6, Q2; Cause and Effect

questions.question_text:
Statements:
I. The Reserve Bank of India has recently put restrictions on a few small banks in the country.
II. The small banks in the in India are not in a position to withstand the competitions of the bigger in the public sector.
Choose the relationship between Statements I and II.

options.A: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect.
options.B: Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect.
options.C: Both statements are effects of some common cause.

questions.explanation: The source notes the RBI's Prompt Corrective Action restrictions. A small bank's inability to withstand competition is evidence of weakness that can prompt regulatory restrictions; the restrictions do not cause the underlying competitive weakness.
questions.source: Analytical Reasoning 02_Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 7, Q3; Cause and Effect

questions.question_text:
Statements:
I. There is an unprecedented increase in the number of young unemployed in comparison to the previous year.
II. A large number of candidates submitted applications against an advertisement for the post of manager issued by a bank.
Choose the relationship between Statements I and II.

options.A: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect.
options.B: Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect.
options.C: Both statements are effects of some common cause.

questions.explanation: A sharp rise in youth unemployment can increase the number of applicants competing for a bank manager vacancy. The applications do not cause the broader unemployment increase.
questions.source: Analytical Reasoning 02_Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 8, Q4; Cause and Effect

questions.question_text:
Statements:
I. The literacy rate in the district has been increasing for the last four years.
II. The district administration has conducted an extensive training programme for the workers involved in the literacy drive.
Choose the relationship between Statements I and II.

options.A: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect.
options.B: Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect.
options.C: Both statements are effects of some common cause.

questions.explanation: Training workers involved in a literacy drive can improve the effectiveness of that drive and contribute to rising literacy. The literacy trend does not explain why the administration conducted the training.
questions.source: Analytical Reasoning 02_Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 9, Q5; Cause and Effect

questions.question_text:
Directions: There is a statement given, which is followed by two arguments. Choose which argument is strong and which is weak among the given arguments.
Q1. Statement: Should parents make the same financial commitment to their kids' marriages as they do to their education?
Arguments:
1. Parents must not put less money into marriage.
2. The future of the kids depends more on parents' investments in education.
questions.explanation: Argument 2 gives a relevant reason to prioritize educational investment because it affects children's future. Argument 1 merely asserts that marriage spending should not be lower and does not support that claim with a relevant reason.
questions.source: Analytical Reasoning 05_Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 4, Q1; Decision Making

questions.question_text:
Directions: There is a statement given, which is followed by two arguments. Choose which argument is strong and which is weak among the given arguments.
Q2. Statement: Should the words 'Cigarette smoking is harmful to your health' actually be included on cigarette packages?
Arguments:
1. To make smokers aware that they are inhaling poison is, in a way, a form of brainwashing.
2. No, it makes smoking less enjoyable.
questions.explanation: Argument 1 addresses the purpose of a health warning by explaining that it informs smokers of a health risk. Argument 2 concerns enjoyment rather than whether the warning should be provided, so it is weak.
questions.source: Analytical Reasoning 05_Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 5, Q2; Decision Making

questions.question_text:
Directions: There is a statement given, which is followed by two arguments. Choose which argument is strong and which is weak among the given arguments.
Q3. Statement: The question is whether adult education programmes should take precedence over those that are required.
Arguments:
1. No. It will also contribute to the success of the mandatory education initiative.
2. Yes. It will aid in the eradication of adult illiteracy.
questions.explanation: Argument 2 identifies adult illiteracy as a direct problem addressed by adult education and supports giving the programme priority. Argument 1 does not explain why adult education should or should not take precedence; it only asserts a possible contribution to another initiative.
questions.source: Analytical Reasoning 05_Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 6, Q3; Decision Making

questions.question_text:
Directions: There is a statement given, which is followed by two arguments. Choose which argument is strong and which is weak among the given arguments.
Q4. Statement: Should all students in secondary school be required to take 'computer knowledge' as a subject?
Arguments:
1. No, we cannot imitate western methods; we need to provide 'bread' for everyone.
2. Yes. Without providing our children with computers, we cannot compete in the global economy.
questions.explanation: Argument 2 gives a relevant connection between computer knowledge and students' ability to participate in a global economy. Argument 1 relies on an unrelated comparison with Western methods and does not show why computer knowledge should not be required.
questions.source: Analytical Reasoning 05_Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 7, Q4; Decision Making
